_comment: How a storefront order should be marked once the yard system has invoiced it. Read by
CoreYard through STORE_ORDER_POLICY_FILE and applied by `bin/coreyard orders
The interesting decision is fulfillment, and it is ours rather than CoreYard's because
it depends on who buys the shipping label.
Shopify has no 'picked but not shipped' state: creating a fulfillment CLOSES the
fulfillment order. ShipStation needs it left open so it can attach the UPS tracking
number when it buys the label — fulfilling a parcel order here would leave the buyer
with no tracking email at all. Freight and pickup-only orders never get a UPS label, so
ShipStation never sees them and nothing else would ever close them out; those we
A mixed order is left open: it still has parcel lines for ShipStation to ship, and
closing it early costs the buyer their tracking.
The groups are the ship:* tags scripts/tag_shipping.py writes from content/freight.json.
Keep the two files in step: a group named here that tag_shipping no longer writes will
silently fall through to the default.
